q: Why does anaerobic respiration in humans yield only 2 ATP per glucose?
options: Pyruvate isn't oxidised further: most energy stays in lactate, so only glycolysis makes ATP
Converting pyruvate into lactate uses up 28 of the 30 ATP molecules that glycolysis produced
Lactate dehydrogenase hydrolyses most of the ATP made during glycolysis back into ADP
Glycolysis uses 4 ATP and makes only 2 ATP whenever oxygen is unavailable to the cell
explanation: Glycolysis makes 4 ATP and uses 2 → net 2. Converting pyruvate to lactate only regenerates NAD+; it makes no ATP. Lactate still holds most of glucose's chemical energy – which is why it can later be converted back to pyruvate and respired aerobically. Without O2 the electron transport chain stops, so there is no oxidative phosphorylation.
